home.title: The Fundraising Game
home.introduction: Get your board members involved in building and executing your organization's fundraising strategy.
paragraphs: Imagine walking into your next board meeting, and every board member comes prepared with answers to some very specific fundraising questions.

Each person has identified who they believe should fund your organization's mission, why those people have a strong reason to give, where to find them, how to attract them, how to raise money from them, what to ask for, how much to ask, and the role they would love to play to support fundraising.
Now imagine what that board meeting would look like.
Each board member presents their recommended fundraising audience and explains why they believe that audience should support your mission.
You all discuss their recommendations, examine the opportunities, and agree on the specific audiences your organization should focus on.
Maybe you agree on one audience. Maybe two. You might even agree to pursue all the audiences recommended.
The important thing is that you have collectively agreed on who your organization will raise money from and exactly how you intend to raise that money.
And before that meeting ends, every board member agrees on the role they will personally play in helping the organization reach those audiences and raise money from them.
Think about what that would mean for your organization.
Think about what it would mean for your board.
Your organization now has a fundraising strategy that identifies who should fund your mission, where to find them, how to attract them, what to ask them for, and how much to ask.
These are the core elements of a fundraising strategy.

And because your board members participated in developing and adopting that strategy, they understand how the organization intends to raise money. They also understand where they fit into the process and what they have agreed to do.
You have a fundraising strategy your board helped build, and board members who are ready to work with you to execute it.
That's what we want to help you accomplish with The Fundraising Game.
We've put together the questions, materials, and tools you need to take your board through this process.

You don't need to hire a professional facilitator. You can lead the process yourself. And if you would prefer to have a professional facilitate your session, we will make a fundraising professional with years of experience available to help.
biography: My name is Rooney A. My mission is to help you raise money exponentially. And maybe transform your board while doing so.
So far I've contributed to raising over $5m based on my strategy and the fundraising assets I create. I've also trained hundreds of nonprofit leaders and fundraisers on sustainable fundraising.

There are two ways we can support you to build a successful fundraising strategy for your organization. You can do it with me alone. This is usually faster, usually within 24 to 48 hours, or you can do it with your board, and still get my help of course. But this could happen as soon as your next board meeting.

The number one reason most organizations struggle to raise money is their fundraising strategy or approach. Once you get it right, with a little focus, time and resource investment, you will begin to see the returns in no time.

how.title: Get Your Board Members Fundraising By Your Next Board Meeting.
how.article:
### Play The Fundraising Game With Your Board.

Imagine going into your next board meeting with every board member prepared to discuss who should fund your organization's mission, how to raise money from them, and the role they can personally play in helping your organization reach its fundraising goal.

Now imagine ending that meeting with a fundraising strategy you all developed and agreed to execute together.

**That's exactly what The Fundraising Game helps you do.**

We've put together the questions, the group meeting platform, and the facilitation guidance you need to make this happen.

You can lead the entire process yourself, even if you're not a fundraising professional.

And at the end, your organization receives the fundraising strategy you and your board members agreed on.

**Play The Fundraising Game With Your Board: $997**

## Here's How The Fundraising Game Works.

### Step 1: Play The Fundraising Game Yourself.

It begins with you.

You'll tell us a little about your organization, including your mission, the people you serve, and the fundraising goal you're working towards.

Then you'll answer five specific fundraising questions.

**Before finishing, we'll ask you one more question:**

"How do you see yourself participating and supporting your organization to reach this fundraising goal?"

Once you've finished, you're ready for step 2.

### Step 2: Invite Your Board Members to Play The Fundraising Game.

Now it's your board members' turn.

You'll enter the date of your upcoming board meeting and invite your board members by providing their names, email addresses, and board roles.

We'll automatically send each person an invitation to play The Fundraising Game.

Each board member will answer the same five fundraising questions you answered.

They will also share how they see themselves participating in and supporting fundraising.



By inviting every member to think about these questions before the meeting, you're giving everyone an opportunity to contribute to the development of your organization's fundraising strategy.

You can see who has responded from your workspace, read their recommendations, and remind anyone who hasn't completed their questions.

As responses arrive, you'll get email notification for each response and begin to see the different fundraising opportunities your board members believe your organization should pursue.

**And now you're ready for the most important part of The Fundraising Game.**

### Step 3: Play The Group Fundraising Game at Your Next Board Meeting.

This is where all the ideas come together.

When your board meets, you'll open The Board Fundraising Game Platform and share the group game link with everyone.

Each board member can follow the discussion on their own device as you click through each board member's recommendation.

As the meeting progresses, you and your board members will decide:

- Which funding audiences your organization will pursuea and focus on.
- Where and how you'll find those audiences.
- How you'll attract their interest daily.
- The process you'll use to raise money from them.
- What you'll ask them to support and how much you'll ask.

Maybe your board agrees to focus on individual donors and grantors. Maybe you decide to pursue businesses as well. You might agree on several audiences, depending on the opportunities you've identified.

The important thing is that you're making those decisions together.

And any new ideas that come up during the meeting can become part of the strategy you adopt.

The platform captures the discussion, so those additional contributions can be included in your final strategy when agreed upon.

**Before the meeting ends, you'll discuss one more important thing: How will each board member participate?**

Remember that everyone already answered how they see themselves supporting fundraising.

Now you'll review those responses and discuss the roles each member is willing to play in executing the strategy you've agreed on.

Someone may agree to help identify potential donors from their network.

Another member may agree to introduce your organization to businesses they already know.

Someone else may be willing to participate in donor meetings, help develop relationships, or support a particular fundraising approach.

Each board member agrees on the role they're comfortable playing.

**Now your organization has a fundraising strategy, and your board members know how they have agreed to help execute it.**

Before closing the group game, everyone gets an opportunity to review and adopt the strategy you've collectively agreed on from their screen.

You can see who has adopted it.

And that completes The Fundraising Game.

### Step 4: Download the Fundraising Strategy You and Your Board Members Agreed On.

After your meeting, we'll put together the fundraising strategy your board adopted.

This is where all the decisions you've made come together in one document.

Your strategy will include a short executive summary of your organization's fundraising goal and the approach you've agreed to pursue.

Then, for every funding audience your board adopted, you'll see:

**Who should fund your mission and why they will give, where to find them**, the approaches your board agreed to use to generate interest in your organization and its mission, The fundraising process your organization will follow to raise money for them, the specific funding requests to ask each audience and the amounts agreed.

We'll also include the new ideas that were introduced and adopted during your discussion, so your final strategy reflects what your board actually agreed on.

And you'll have a record of the fundraising responsibilities your board members accepted.

**We won't create another strategy for you. We'll give you the strategy you and your board members developed and adopted together, professionally organized and ready to use.**

You'll be able to add your organization's logo and brand colors before downloading the finished strategy.

We'll email you when it's ready, and you'll be able to download it from your workspace.

You'll also have a shareable link and an email you can copy and send to your board members.

So everyone can have the same strategy that you collectively agreed to execute.

## Now Imagine What Happens After That Board Meeting.

Your board members know who your organization's ideal funding audiences are.

They understand why those audiences should support your mission.

They know where to look for potential funders and how your organization intends to attract them.

They understand the process you've agreed to use to raise money, including what to ask for and how much.

And they know the role they've personally agreed to play.

**Now they can begin looking within their own networks, relationships, and communities to identify people who fit the funding audiences you've adopted.**

They can begin contributing to the fundraising activities you agreed on.

And when you meet again, you have an actual fundraising strategy to guide your discussions about progress.

Think about the difference between that and a board meeting where fundraising comes up, everyone talks about the need for more money, and the meeting ends without an agreed approach.

## Your Board Members Don't Have to Be Fundraising Experts.

They just need to be willing to think about who should fund your mission and how they could help your organization reach those people.

The Fundraising Game provides the questions that help them think through those opportunities.

And when it's time to meet, we'll provide the platform and facilitation guidance to help you discuss their recommendations and agree on a strategy.

You can guide your own board through the process.

If you need assistance, you can ask for help from your workspace.

## What You're Getting for $997

**The complete Fundraising Game experience for your organization.**

Your purchase includes:

- Access to the five fundraising questions for you and your board members, with the ability to write or speak your answers.
- Individual invitations for board members, with a workspace for reviewing responses and preparing for your meeting.
- The live Group Fundraising Game platform, including guided discussions, meeting transcription, and strategy adoption.
- A final fundraising strategy reflecting the audiences, approaches, and decisions your board collectively adopted, including the agreed responsibilities.
- A branded strategy document you can download and share with your board members.

**One payment: $997.**

## Are You Ready to Make Your Next Board Meeting Different?

Imagine ending your next board meeting with a fundraising strategy that answers the most important questions about how your organization intends to raise money.

Imagine your board members understanding that strategy because they helped develop it.

And imagine every member leaving the meeting knowing how they have agreed to contribute towards reaching your fundraising goal.

That's what we've built The Fundraising Game to help you accomplish.

**Your next board meeting could be where your board finally starts working with you to raise money.**

### Play The Fundraising Game With Your Board.

**$997 | One-time payment**
